title: Schedule Three-View Browsing and Crew Parity
lede: List, Week, and Calendar now share one stable date context, complete responsive browsing, and the same safe staff crew setup and versioned editing model.

stats.n: A Week or Calendar date no longer leaks into a fresh List entry
Events, active days, and open slots are visible for Sep. 21–27
The full 55-event September agenda works at 390px
List, Week, and Calendar now share setup and focused management

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Each pair uses the same authenticated Admin role, source data, period, filters, viewport, and scroll position. Production is the read-only baseline; local is the changed build.

pairs.title: Today is an explicit List boundary
pairs.sub: The continuous timeline now explains the reading direction and keeps the sticky boundary stable.
pairs.beforeCap: Today appeared as a badge with no explanation of what lived above or below it.
pairs.afterCap: Today now names the continuous model: past above, upcoming below.

pairs.title: Past events are no longer mislabeled as archived
pairs.sub: Normal ended crew groups remain live timeline history; only genuinely archived calendar records use archive language.
pairs.beforeCap: Ordinary August events repeated an Archived label and the Today return did not show direction.
pairs.afterCap: False archive labels are gone and the return control points toward Today.

pairs.title: Week is a readable staffing board
pairs.sub: The same Sep. 21–27 week is shown at 1280 × 900 with all venue filters enabled.
pairs.beforeCap: Names truncate almost immediately, day orientation is split from navigation, and staffing needs require decoding tiny dots and fractions.
pairs.afterCap: One shared period header names the week and totals; cards expose time, venue, title, coverage, open slots, and Your shift.

pairs.title: Calendar cells carry useful detail
pairs.sub: The same September 2026 month is shown at 1280 × 900 with all venue filters enabled.
pairs.beforeCap: Dense single-line rows clip event identity and leave the operator to infer the day's load.
pairs.afterCap: Day counts, readable time/title chips, and coverage tags make the month scannable; phone widths use a complete agenda.

pairs.title: Week can start an unconfigured crew in place
pairs.sub: The same authenticated Admin, Sep. 7–13 period, source data, viewport, and unconfigured Women’s Golf event are shown before and after.
pairs.beforeCap: The unconfigured event was only a link to Event detail, so Week could not begin staffing work.
pairs.afterCap: The event now opens a focused staff sheet with deliberate Home, Away, and empty starting points, while Event detail stays one link away.

pairs.title: Calendar uses the identical crew setup contract
pairs.sub: The same authenticated Admin, September 2026 month, source data, viewport, and unconfigured Women’s Golf event are shown before and after.
pairs.beforeCap: The unconfigured month chip only navigated away, leaving Calendar without a staffing entry point.
pairs.afterCap: The month chip now opens the same setup sheet as Week and List; the sheet becomes full-screen and remains usable at 390px.

changes.h: A stress-test week leaked into List
changes.was: Entering List from a standalone Week or Calendar period could land on Sep. 21 instead of the current day.
changes.now: Standalone period-to-List navigation clears period reading anchors and goes to Today; only a genuine List-origin round trip restores the earlier List place.

changes.h: Rapid view toggles could rehydrate stale URL state
changes.was: A fast Week → Calendar → Week sequence could let an older router update replace the user's newer period choice.
changes.now: The active period is handed between views immediately and owned URL writes are recognized before the router round trip, with filters retained.

changes.h: Week compressed the work into fragments
changes.was: Small cards truncated event identity and hid useful coverage, open-slot, venue, and personal-shift context.
changes.now: The shared period header, day counts, readable event cards, explicit staffing state, and expanded mobile days make Week independently useful.

changes.was: Phone widths replaced the month with a recommendation to switch views.
changes.now: Calendar keeps the desktop grid and adds a complete active-day mobile agenda with matching event, coverage, and open-slot semantics.

changes.h: Scope changes could show the wrong rows
changes.was: A server-backed view or sport change could temporarily display prior-scope events under newly selected controls.
changes.now: Only compatible older-record expansion keeps existing rows; every other scope uses an honest geometry-preserving loading state.

changes.h: Week and Calendar stopped at read-only context
changes.was: Configured events opened the legacy detail panel and unconfigured events navigated away, so staff could not complete the List crew workflow from either period view.
changes.now: All three views use one focused staff sheet backed by the existing versioned editor. Unconfigured events offer Home, Away, or empty setup; List keeps its inline multi-event workstation as well.

verification: 84 focused Schedule contracts pass across timeline restoration, three-view behavior, staff/worker boundaries, configured and unconfigured parity, URL state, and UI polish.
Full TypeScript and full ESLint pass for the shared repository state.
Production-shaped app build completes successfully across all 251 static pages.

Authenticated local browser matrices pass List focused-sheet and inline handoffs, Week/Calendar configured and unconfigured routing, Home/All filtering, view round-trips, Escape close/reopen, period retention, and 390px setup sheets without horizontal overflow.

Runtime failure found: the shared configured working editor reaches its existing endpoint, but Preview returns Prisma P2022 because the generated client expects a column missing from the Preview database. No schedule data was mutated; full editor-control runtime proof remains blocked by that environment drift.
notes: The baselines are read-only captures of the currently deployed Schedule using the same authenticated role, data, periods, and viewports as the local after captures; no production or Preview schedule data was mutated.

Configured crew actions route to the new shared sheet in all three views. Assignment, slot, conversion, call-window, and recovery controls remain source-verified but could not be exercised locally until the Preview schema catches up with the current Prisma client.
This review proves the local implementation only. It was not committed, pushed, deployed, or production-verified.
